assumptions.assumption: Unmapped moving objects will be detected by lidar within 1.0 m before they become a collision threat
assumptions.why: first_not_on_map shows detection at >1.9 m; reactive evasion only triggers at d<1.0 m, which is too late

assumptions.assumption: Backing away at 0.4 m/s for 0.5 s provides enough clearance
assumptions.why: back distance ≈0.2 m, but closing speeds up to 0.75 m/s leave insufficient margin

assumptions.assumption: Rotating in place at ≤1.0 rad/s can reorient the robot away before impact
assumptions.why: rotation may require >1 s while the object is already <1 m away

assumptions.assumption: Clearance‑hold keeps the robot stopped until the object is safely beyond 2.0 m
assumptions.why: collisions occur while robot is stopped, indicating the hold released before the object cleared

assumptions.assumption: The VO planner will avoid any collision if a feasible trajectory exists
assumptions.why: VO selects commands that still lead to collisions with unmapped points not represented as tracks

approach_families.family: Simple pause_until based on distance & shrinking

approach_families.result: mixed (4/7 passes overall), still collisions in many runs

candidates.idea: Aggressive raw‑TTC based full stop with an extended clearance‑hold: when any unmapped point yields TTC < 1.0 s, command an immediate stop and keep the robot halted until the point stays beyond 2.5 m for at least 1 s, ignoring VO and other layers.
candidates.for: prevent collisions when a fast‑approaching object is detected early
candidates.risk: may increase stall time and reduce overall throughput

candidates.idea: Increase reactive‑evasion thresholds: trigger at d < 1.5 m, use back‑up speed 0.8 m/s for 1.0 s, and rotate at up to 1.5 rad/s; also enlarge the cool‑down to avoid repeated triggers.
candidates.for: give the robot more time and distance to separate from the object
candidates.risk: could cause unnecessary stops or overshoot in tight corridors

candidates.idea: Add a raw‑TTC gating layer before the VO planner: scan unmapped points within a ±30° forward cone, compute TTC for each, and if any TTC < 0.8 s force a stop (or short backup) and skip VO; resume VO only after TTC > 1.5 s for 0.5 s.
candidates.for: ensure VO never selects a command that would intersect a fast‑approaching unmapped object
candidates.risk: may increase the number of stop episodes if the TTC threshold is too aggressive

diagnosis.chosen: Candidate 3 is chosen because it directly blocks unsafe VO commands using an inexpensive raw‑TTC check, integrates cleanly with the existing VO pipeline, and addresses the core failure where unmapped points are not represented in VO tracks.
diagnosis.target: controller (add raw‑TTC gating before _vo_planner) and a small helper function _raw_ttc_gate
diagnosis.direction: 1. Implement _raw_ttc_gate(st, pose) that extracts unmapped points via _unmapped_raw, filters those within a ±30° forward cone, and computes TTC = d / (max(rel_speed,0.1)+_MAX_OBJECT_SPEED). 2. In controller(), after _perceive and before any VO or speed logic, call _raw_ttc_gate; if it returns a pause duration, set st['pause_until']=max(st.get('pause_until',-1.0), t+pause) and return (0.0,0.0,False). 3. While paused, keep the clearance‑hold active (call _arm_clear_hold) so the robot stays stopped. 4. Only when t >= st['pause_until'] and the TTC of all forward points exceeds 1.5 s for 0.5 s, clear the pause flag and resume normal VO/predictive‑speed flow. 5. Ensure _guard is still applied to any backup command issued during the pause. 6. Tune the TTC thresholds (0.8 s for stop, 1.5 s for resume) based on observed closing speeds.
